title: Choose a mentor who is a facilitator
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Who could you call, just to ask a question?

groups.heading: A game that opened a door

lines.text: Jose said the two brothers got into a routine: pick a person out of the newspaper and cold-call them for fun. The one who was more introverted did not want to call, so his brother did.
They lowered the perception of the risk, he said, by making it almost like prank calls. It is a big deal and a big initiative, and he chases this mentor, cold calling him.

One of those calls reached an executive who opened the door to them, and even offered them a job at the bank. A successful mentor will open the door, Jose said, because they know how hard it was to get there.

As you choose mentors, he said, you never want one who says: you depend on me, or who has an inflated ego and says: I'm the source of this information. You want a mentor who is a facilitator and a servant leader: I can help you as much as you are able to absorb from me, and as much as I am able to give.

All of us have limitations, he said. So take a little of what you want from a mentor and go on and find another one. If anybody tells you: you need me, you need me to do this, run as fast as you can the other way.

It is the same with parents, he said. He is afraid of a father or mother who makes their child dependent on them. You want to teach your child to be independent. Making a child dependent is basically being selfish.
There is a saying he loves and repeats: it is not what you do for your children, but what you have taught them to do for themselves that will make them successful.

That is why you get a mentor, Jose said: it shortens the time it takes to find out whether something has value. And not just any mentor: someone with knowledge in your space. Pick the ideal mentor for you.
A student said that calling people up just for fun shows an entrepreneurial spirit, and that the mother believing in him mattered.
Who is your ideal mentor, and what will you ask first?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the kind of person who would be your ideal mentor.
Write three questions you would ask them.
Write one way you could lower the risk of the first call.
Write one sign that a mentor wants you dependent on them.
Write one thing you are teaching someone to do for themselves.

check.q: What kind of mentor did Jose say you want?
choices: A boss who decides for you

check.q: What did Jose say to do if someone says: you need me?
What kind of mentor did Jose say to pick?
choices: Someone with knowledge in your space

recap: Choose a facilitator who has knowledge in your space. Teach independence.
